_comment: Business vocabulary → Priority screens, for natural-language questions.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A screen's meaning lives in its Hebrew title, and that
title is Priority's wording, not the user's. Someone asks about 'מחזור' and the
screen is 'חשבוניות מס'; asks about 'זיכוי' and ranking puts 'נקודות זיכוי'
above 'חשבוניות זיכוי'. No string matching bridges that, because the words
genuinely differ. Both SAP (synonyms) and Oracle (annotations + glossary) treat
this mapping as the decisive input to natural-language accuracy.
MAINTAIN IT BY HAND. A wrong entry sends the model confidently to the wrong
screen, which is worse than no entry. Every screen name below was checked
against the live dictionary; tests/live.glossary.ts re-checks them all and
fails on any name that does not exist, so add entries and run it.
FIELDS. term = the canonical Hebrew phrase. aliases = other spellings people
actually type, including English and singular/plural variants. screens = best
first. columns = where the value lives. notes = anything a caller must know
BEFORE trusting these screens for this term — read the CINVOICES note as the
example of why this field matters.

terms.notes: Sales revenue lives across FOUR invoice screens, not one, and totalling only AINVOICES understates it. CINVOICES is 'חשבוניות מרכזות' (consolidated) — it can restate amounts already counted in the others, so adding all four together may double-count. Ask which document types the question means. Also: any of them can be in a foreign currency, so group by currency and never add currencies together.
AINVOICES is the header; AINVOICEITEMS is the line detail and is a sub-form of it, reachable via expand or a keyed path.
Invoice and receipt in one document; also carries the payment lines.
Export invoices. Usually foreign currency — read each row's currency rather than assuming.

SALECREDITINVOICES is a SUB-FORM of SALES and has no entity set — reading it directly returns 404. Note the trap this entry exists to prevent: CINVOICES looks like 'credit invoices' and is in fact consolidated invoices, and a plain search for 'זיכוי' ranks 'נקודות זיכוי' (tax credit points) above this.
ORDERS is 'הזמנות'. ORDERITEMS holds the lines and is a sub-form of it.
An approved purchase order cannot be changed on PORDERS; Priority's own help points to PORDERS_CHANGES for that.
PART is the catalogue; LOGPART is 'כרטיס פריט'. Note that Priority calls this screen 'מוצרים' while users usually say 'פריטים'.

PARTBAL is 'מלאי נוכחי במחסנים'. It is published as an entity set but has been observed REFUSING reads with 'לא ניתן להפעיל API למסך זה' — if that happens the screen must be opened for the API in Priority, and it is not a naming problem.
A sub-form of OBLIGO, so read it through the parent. Searching 'חוב' alone also surfaces AGEDEBTS_WORKAREA, which is a scratch work area rather than the ledger.
Note that 'כרטיס חשבון' finds nothing by title search — this entry is the only route to it.
FNCITEMS is 'פירוט התנועה', a sub-form of FNCTRANS.
MAKEPARTCOST is 'תמחיר פריטי יצור' (manufactured), RAWPARTCOST is 'תמחיר ח"ג' (raw materials). Which one depends on the item.
